video.title: He Makes $16K/Month Renting Out a Space He Doesn’t Own

summary: Justin Hall (The Hall ATL) rented a 3,000 sq ft former church unit in a Stone Mountain, Georgia strip mall and converted it into an event venue for birthdays, baby showers, repasses, anniversaries, weddings and fashion shows, while keeping his 9-5 job. He claims about $16K/month average revenue (about 50% net margin) with only his wife helping. Key tactics: organic build-in-public Instagram, cheap Facebook/Instagram ad specials, direct mail aimed at milestone birthdays, a QR-code photo wall that generates repeat leads, and recurring Sunday church rentals that cover rent. Main takeaways: parking, zoning/licensing and lease terms matter more than the building, and local competitors' weak marketing and booking systems are the opening. All figures are self-reported and unverified.

speakers.name: Justin Hall
speakers.description: Founder of The Hall ATL event venue in Stone Mountain, Georgia; technical PM with a 9-5; former DJ and iPhone-repair/studio owner (per host/guest remarks)

ideas.name: Rented strip-mall event venue (The Hall ATL)
ideas.one_liner: Lease a 3,000 sq ft retail unit, build it out cheaply, and rent it by the 6-hour block for parties, weddings and other events.
ideas.business_model: Per-event venue rental with tiered packages and upsells (screens, decor, linens, step-and-repeat, standees); deposits; monthly church rentals.
ideas.customer: Locals in a 5-7 mile radius: people aged 50-70 for milestone birthdays, baby showers, repasses, anniversaries, weddings; East African, Mexican and apartment-dwelling communities; churches.
ideas.problem: People want a venue that is easy to book, looks good, and handles decor/convenience; existing venues are low-tech, poorly marketed and double-book.
ideas.offer: Furnished event hall with LED wall, screens, tables/chairs, prep kitchen with warmers, security, plus decor packages; the pitch is convenience, not just space.

pricing.model: Tiered 6-hour packages plus weekday discounts and monthly church rates
pricing.notes: Gold package ran as a $1,000 special in ads, booking about 10 in a day. Friend in Virginia charges roughly double (over $3,000 for bare-bones).

acquisition_channels.details: New venue Instagram page with build-in-public videos (pulling carpet, kids painting, building DJ booth/chafing table/bar); this alone produced about 10 events before opening and could have produced about 50. Church-space posts outperform everything else.

quote.text: videos of us pulling up carpet or my kids in there with paint brushes outperformed all the other
quote.speaker: Justin Hall

acquisition_channels.details: Facebook/Instagram ads with static images of package specials; initially targeted 22 miles out, now only 5-7 miles around the venue's zip. Led to tours 6 days a week.

quote.text: That was less than $100 in ad spend.
quote.speaker: Justin Hall

acquisition_channels.details: Every door direct mail using driver's-licence-derived birthday data to hit people 3 months before 50/55/60 milestone birthdays, three touches at about 50 cents each; ROI not yet measured.
Instant Spotlight QR photo wall at events captures guests' phone/email into a funnel; about 8% of photo-uploading guests book their own event; Google review request after each event.

quote.text: my latest numbers is about 8%of those people have have booked stuff
quote.speaker: Justin Hall

acquisition_channels.details: Community-specific marketing (Somali, Ethiopian ads and flyers); one bridal shower led to about 10 events from the same community. Also targets apartment complexes.
Free or discounted networking events for Chamber of Commerce; designer fashion shows; preferred caterer list.

ideas.delivery: Justin personally sets up tables, does the walk-through and checklist at start and end of every event, and handles upsold screens/decor; his wife meets clients, runs questionnaires and designs decor visuals. No staff; bookings and tours run through GoHighLevel. Caterers supply food.
unit_economics_claims: Average revenue about $16K/month, best month $22.5K, first month $11K
About 70% margin on a $4,000 event, about 90% on a $1,000 event
Rent $3,000 growing to $4,500, then $5,500 with the new unit; insurance $2,400-2,500/year
Tour close rate about 70%, show rate about 50%
ideas.startup_cost: Build-out about $20-30K; furniture about $5K; Justin says it could be done for under $3,000 with a rent-free period, or about $6,000 including first month's rent and deposit. Licensing and permits delays added costs.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Lease signed Aug 2024; about 10 pre-opening events within roughly a year; official opening Nov 2025 with $11K in the first month. Permits took 6+ months.

acquisition.how: Paid social and Google review loops and the QR photo funnel can be run by agents; direct mail and organic content are tooling-assisted, and tours are in person.

onboarding.how: GoHighLevel handles booking and tour scheduling and contracts; wife's questionnaire/design consult is human.

delivery.how: Physical venue: setup, walk-throughs, cleaning, damage checks and decor all done by humans on site.

billing.how: Deposits and package payments can be handled by online payment and booking software.

support.how: Inquiries and tour bookings can be automated, but day-of issues and customer handling are in person.

uk_applicability.notes: Model works in the UK (retail-unit conversions, social marketing, birthday targeting) but needs premises licence/TENs for alcohol and music, fire risk assessment, change-of-use planning, business rates, and commercial lease negotiation. Every Door Direct Mail with licence-derived birthday data is US-specific; UK direct mail needs GDPR-compliant data. Prices and church demand will differ.

risks: Landlord and zoning refusals; permits and licences can delay opening by 6+ months
No non-compete clause in lease allowed four competitors into the same plaza
Property damage, spills and cultural incidents (e.g. animal slaughter)
Fixed rent with seasonal gaps; weekday demand is weak
Founder runs it part-time on top of a 9-5 and is present at every event
Liability from large events, alcohol and fire

ideas.name: Recurring church space rental
ideas.one_liner: Rent the hall every Sunday to small churches at a flat monthly fee, covering the venue's rent.
ideas.business_model: Monthly recurring rental, with optional livestream upgrade.
ideas.customer: Small churches (15-40 members) lacking their own building.
ideas.problem: Small congregations need an affordable weekly meeting space.
ideas.offer: Sunday time blocks (about 3 hours) in the hall, with an optional $1,800/month package including PTZ cameras and livestream training.

pricing.notes: Three churches currently pay about $1,000/month each.

acquisition_channels.details: Organic Instagram posts about church space being available outperform all other content and generate the most phone calls.

quote.text: my ads on church space well outperform everything else
quote.speaker: Justin Hall

ideas.delivery: Provide the room on Sunday slots; two spaces used simultaneously; optional livestream training.
unit_economics_claims: Three churches at about $1,000/month cover the rent

acquisition.how: Organic and paid posts and inbound calls; an agent could handle enquiries and listings.

delivery.how: Physical space must be opened, set up and maintained.

billing.how: Recurring monthly payments are easily automated.

support.how: Occasional requests for extra time handled by humans.

uk_applicability.notes: UK has many small churches seeking hire space; requires hirer agreement and possibly licence terms.

risks: Ad hoc requests for extra weekday time

quotes.text: I have three churches right now that are every Sunday.
quotes.speaker: Justin Hall

ideas.name: Dedicated church-space rental business
ideas.one_liner: Run a generic church-style building rented to churches during the week, with more access for services, study and offices.
ideas.problem: Many small churches need a place and office days
ideas.offer: A generic, church-like building shared by multiple churches

acquisition_channels.details: Organic posts about church space performed best.

ideas.delivery: Provide the building; not yet tested as a standalone business.

uk_applicability.notes: Plausible, but UK property use and licensing apply.

quotes.text: maybe there's a business into just having a open space
quotes.speaker: Justin Hall

tactics.name: Build in public on a fresh Instagram page
steps: Create a new venue-specific Instagram account
Post renovation videos (pulling carpet, kids painting, building the DJ booth, bar, chafing table)
Convert personal followers to the page
Have pricing ready since enquiries arrive before opening
Offer the unfinished venue at a discount to start earning

tactics.name: Package-special Facebook ad blitz
steps: Create static ads for a discounted decor package (e.g. gold package at $1,000 instead of $2,800)
Geo-target 5-7 miles around the venue
Book tours and close about 70%

tactics.name: Milestone-birthday direct mail
steps: Pull lists of people turning 50/55/60
Start mailing 3 months before the birthday
Send three touches at about 50 cents each
Use custom birthday cards from the hall

tactics.name: QR-code photo wall referral loop
steps: Place QR codes on pillars, tables and screens
Guests upload selfies shown on the LED wall, entering phone and email
Add a tipping feature for the guest of honour
Send the full gallery afterwards with a Google review request
Market to captured leads; about 8% book

tactics.name: Pre-sell with personalised mockups
steps: Have clients fill out a questionnaire
Create screen visuals with their colours and photos before the tour
Show them on screens when they arrive to sell the transformation

tactics.name: Negotiate free rent for build-out
steps: Submit a detailed business plan to landlord
Ask for months of free rent while building out (he got 4-6 months)
Check there's no clause allowing competing venues

tactics.name: Source furniture cheaply
steps: Buy tables on Facebook Marketplace/Craigslist for about $30 vs $120 retail
Spend about $5K on all tables and chairs

tactics.name: Fill weekdays
steps: Offer $450 blank canvas Monday-Thursday
Give free networking events to Chamber of Commerce
Target corporate events at reduced rates

warnings.warning: Don't fall in love with the property; parking, county zoning and liquor licence rules matter more.

quote.text: don't fall in love with the property. You can have the most beautiful property that has horrible parking.
quote.speaker: Justin Hall

warnings.warning: Ensure the lease has non-compete protection; four rival venues moved into his plaza.

quote.text: Nothing was in our lease that said you could not have another event venue.
quote.speaker: Justin Hall

warnings.warning: Get written confirmation on licences; a wrong answer on an entertainment licence cost four months.

quote.text: They really did require entertainment license.
quote.speaker: Justin Hall

warnings.warning: Perfectionism delayed launch and burned rent; launch earlier.

quote.text: we're losing so much money because we're paying rent in this empty building essentially.
quote.speaker: Justin Hall

warnings.warning: Put no-open-flame and animal rules in the contract and hold deposits; a goat was slaughtered in the venue.

quote.text: But we've had to add it to our contract.
quote.speaker: Justin Hall

warnings.warning: A full wedding for $3,500 was unprofitable; underpricing early.

quote.text: we gave somebody a full wedding and reception for $3,500.
quote.speaker: Justin Hall

lessons.lesson: Low-tech, poorly marketed incumbents are an opportunity: simple online booking, social presence and fast follow-up beat them.

quote.text: One doesn't even have a website.
quote.speaker: Justin Hall

lessons.lesson: Rent rather than buy; asset-light venue businesses need little capital.
Fixed overhead makes margins rise with revenue; fill capacity with higher-priced packages and upsells.
Sell convenience and transformation, not square footage.

quote.text: We're not selling the space, we're selling convenience.
quote.speaker: Justin Hall

lessons.lesson: Launch imperfect and start earning; early demand arrived before the venue was finished.
Recurring tenants such as churches stabilise cash flow and cover fixed rent.
Customers can be the marketing: every guest is a lead if you capture contact info and offer a reason to share.
Local relationships with regulators (showing up with muffins) can unblock permitting delays.
Focus ads tightly on a 5-7 mile radius rather than a whole metro area.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with specific numbers and process details, but the business is under a year old and all figures are self-reported and unverified; ROI on direct mail not measured and some revenue/profit figures are rough.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Justin offers a free ebook via Instagram; no major sponsor conflict beyond the host's Beehiiv sponsor read.
